title: Training for Public Service Staff in Procurement and Measures to Tackle Recurrent IT Lapses Highlighted in Auditor-General's Reports
what_it_is: Training for Public Service Staff in Procurement and Measures to Tackle Recurrent IT Lapses Highlighted in Auditor-General's Reports

sections.label: IT control lapses in public service
sections.summary: Asked whether recurring IT control lapses in the Auditor-General's Report reflect systemic issues in the public service and what measures will address the weaknesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance in view of the recurring lapses in IT controls highlighted in the latest Auditor-General's Report, whether there are inherent systemic issues within the public service and what effective measures will be taken to address the weaknesses.

sections.label: Tool deployment timeline
sections.summary: SNDGG has piloted a tool with some agencies, deploying it progressively from January 2021, fully for high-priority systems by December 2022 and remaining systems by December 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: SNDGG has started a pilot with some agencies and the tool will be progressively deployed from January 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This will be fully implemented for high-priority systems by December 2022 and all remaining systems by December 2023.

sections.label: Enhancing user account solution
sections.summary: SNDGG is enhancing the solution to trigger automatic removal of unneeded accounts and review of access rights, implemented for 800 high-priority systems by December 2023 and remaining systems by December 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: SNDGG is in the midst of enhancing this solution, so that it can trigger automatic removal of unneeded user accounts and review of user access rights, once the staff movement or role change is updated in the HR records.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This system will be implemented for 800 high-priority systems by December 2023 and all remaining systems by December 2024.

sections.label: Leadership competencies and performance reviews
sections.summary: Leadership competencies and responsibilities are conveyed to senior Public Service leaders, evaluated in performance reviews, and those who fall short are rated less favourably.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: These expectations are spelt out in the form of leadership competencies and responsibilities, which are conveyed to all senior Public Service leaders in Ministries and Statutory Boards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We evaluate our leaders against these expectations as part of their performance reviews and those who fall short will be rated less favourably.

sections.label: Agencies investigating Auditor-General lapses
sections.summary: Agencies mentioned in the Auditor-General's report are conducting further investigation into the lapses where warranted, and written answers and postponed questions are noted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Where warranted, agencies mentioned in the Auditor-General’s report are conducting further investigation into the lapses.
